text: Short ENIGMA strain names are not globally unique. MT20 linked a groundwater Rhodanobacter glycinis isolate to a clinical Streptococcus pneumoniae record, contaminating genus–environment profiles; the cited GTDB match involved 8,434 genomes, 1,751 clinical.

text: In Web of Microbes observations, action codes I and E define the binary produced category used in NB02 and NB08; N and D do not. The raw action code is not itself a produced/consumed label.

A naive `SELECT action` gives you the raw code; it does NOT give you a binary produced/consumed label. The binary definition used in NB02 and NB08 is `produced = action IN ('I', 'E')` — a compound is counted as produced when it either increased in supernatant (was there and more accumulated) or emerged (was below the detection limit and reached it).

Lower to `min_annotated=2` (still valid with FDR correction) and include PFam domains (814 terms with 2+ genes) alongside TIGRFam (88 terms). This increases module annotation from 8% to 80%.

text: Fitness Browser sequence-download and gene-table locus tags can differ: Dyella79 had 0% overlap, whereas other examined organisms had >94%; unchecked joins of DIAMOND hits can silently yield zero matches.

If you build DIAMOND databases from aaseqs and then try to join the hit locusIds back to the gene table, the join will silently produce zero matches. Check locusId overlap between datasets before analysis. Affected: Dyella79 (0% overlap). Other organisms had >94% overlap.
heading: FB Locus Tag Mismatch Between Gene Table and Aaseqs Download

text: Across 45 Fitness Browser tables, no explicit essentiality or insertion flag was found. Absence of type='1' genes from `genefitness` supplies only an upper bound on true essentiality, not a confirmed essential-gene call.
quote: **[conservation_vs_fitness]** After checking all 45 tables in `kescience_fitnessbrowser`, there is no explicit essentiality column, insertion count, or "has fitness data" flag. The `gene.type` column encodes feature type (1=CDS, 5=pseudo, 7=rRNA, 2=tRNA), not essentiality. To identify putative essential genes, compare the `gene` table (type='1') against `genefitness` — genes absent from genefitness had no viable transposon mutants. This is an upper bound on true essentiality.
heading: FB Gene Table Has No Essentiality Flag

text: For representative FASTA extraction across 154 clades, 5000-row OFFSET batches were orders of magnitude slower than one partition-filtered query per clade.

For extracting cluster rep FASTAs across 154 clades, paginated queries (5000 rows per batch) were orders of magnitude slower than single queries per clade. Since `gene_cluster` is partitioned by `gtdb_species_clade_id`, a single `WHERE gtdb_species_clade_id = 'X'` query per clade is fast. Only paginate when the result set would exceed memory.
heading: Spark LIMIT/OFFSET Pagination Is Slow

text: Core-gene percentages depend on whether unmapped genes are included: the cited essential-gene example is 82% with all genes versus 86% with mapped genes only; cross-project comparisons must retain the denominator.

Different projects may use different denominators. This caused a critical review issue where figures showed 86%/78% but prose said 82%/66%. Always document which denominator is used, and be consistent within a synthesis or comparison.

# Try original ID first, then stripped, then partial match
